names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 27 martie; the troparion page spells her «Matroana».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 27 Μαρτίου, «Αγία Ματρώνα η εν Θεσσαλονίκη», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 27 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Света мученица Матрона.“, with Света left off, which is not a rank, and with the rank word мученица left off. The heading gives no epithet and no city — Thessalonica is in the body's first sentence — so the bare forename is what the source gives; no other folder in the corpus holds a Serbian Матрона.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2614 is «Матрона Солунская (Фессалоникийская), мц.»; the form stored here is the one the day line itself uses, with the rank word left off, and the page's parenthesis is the same city under its other name.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 марта ст. ст. — «Мц. Матроны Солунской (III-IV)»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows on this folder already keep, and name page 2614 gives «День памяти: 27 марта» and nothing else, so no second day is owed. The calendar dates her «III-IV», the third or fourth century, and carries the fullest life of her this folder has had; it is set down below. The day page prints no troparion or kontakion at all, for her or for anybody on the day. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 27 martie — «Sfânta Muceniță Matrona din Tesalonic»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 27ης Μαρτίου — «Αγία Ματρώνα η εν Θεσσαλονίκη»

attestations.note: The page gives the fullest account of her on any calendar the corpus has read: the name of her mistress, Παντίλλα or Παυτίλλα, wife of the commander of the garrison of Thessalonica; the informer among the household slaves; the three imprisonments; the fourteen days of hunger; the oaken stocks; Στρατόνικος, who was ordered to wrap the body in a hide and throw it outside the walls; the burial beside the Egnatian Way; the translation into the city by Alexander, bishop of Thessalonica, who built a church for her; a monastery of hers outside the walls; and the removal of the body to Barcelona under Frankish rule, to a church destroyed in the Second World War. It gives no year, and the second couplet it prints fixes only the day, «Εἰκάδι ἑβδομάτῃ θάνε Ματρῶνα ἑνὶ εἱρκτῇ» — on the twenty-seventh Matrona died in prison. It prints an apolytikion, which is added to this folder.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.04.2026 (27. март ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Матрона.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same woman: an orphan girl who was a servant in a Jewish household at Thessalonica, starved to death for going to church instead of the synagogue and thrown from the roof of the house. The entry gives no year, no century, no reign and no persecutor, so this folder's empty `dates` object stays empty, as it was. Two things in it are new to the folder and one of them is a reading left open. It has her mistress die by falling from the same place on the house from which she had thrown Matrona's body. And it says that a bishop Alexander, learning of the many wonders at her grave, built a church over it. **That bishop was not identified and takes no row and no relation.** The corpus holds `alexander-of-thessalonica`, archbishop of that city in the third and fourth centuries and a father of the First Council, who may well be the man; but the Prologue gives this Alexander no see at all, and an identification on a bare forename and a city the entry gives the martyr rather than the bishop is a guess. It is named in the range's report for the author. The stored form is the bare forename, because Света is not a rank and мученица is the rank this folder's `types` carry; Thessalonica is the corpus's own way of telling her from the other Matronas and is not in the heading. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Matroana, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un Milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Muceniţe Matroana din Tesalonic

english.text: Thy ewe-lamb, O Jesus, Matrona, cries out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking Thee I am in torment; I am crucified with Thee and buried with Thee in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thee, that I may reign in Thee; I die for Thee, that I may live for Thee. Receive me, then, as an unblemished sacrifice, who offer myself to Thee in love. At her prayers, since Thou art merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Γνώμην ἀήττητον, Ματρώνα φέρουσα, πίστιν τὴν ἔνθεον, ἄσυλον ἔσωσας, μὴ δουλωθεῖσα τὴν ψυχήν, Ἑβραίων τὴ ἀπηνεία ὅθεν ἀριστεύσασα, καὶ τὸν δόλιον κτείνασα, μυστικῶς νενύμφευσαι, τῷ Δεσπότῃ τῆς κτίσεως. Αὐτὸν οὒν ἐκτενῶς ἐκδυσώπει, πάσης ἠμᾶς ρυσθήναι βλάβης.

source.text: saint.gr — Αγία Ματρώνα η εν Θεσσαλονίκη, Ἀπολυτίκιον. Recorded with kind troparion, which is the schema's word for it.

english.text: Bearing an unconquered mind, O Matrona, you kept the faith that is of God inviolate, not enslaving your soul to the harshness of the Hebrews; wherefore, having proved yourself valiant and slain the deceiver, you were mystically betrothed to the Master of creation. Entreat him earnestly, then, that we may be delivered from every hurt.
